predecessors.name: Ghurid dynasty
predecessors.text: Bihar (subjugated 'in 1200') and Bengal, taken by Bakhtiyar as the Ghurid general in eastern India

successors.name: Mamluk dynasty of Delhi
successors.text: Lakhnauti (Gaur), the Rarh and Varendra country of the old Sena kingdom (the mamluk-dynasty dossier's region for 1225-1227)

ledger.x: 1206: the Khalji state of Lakhnauti stands as its own after Muhammad of Ghor's death.
1225: Iltutmish invades Bengal and Ghiyasuddin Iwaz submits.
1227: the Khalji kingdom of Bengal ends.
1227: the tribute ends with the fall of Lakhnauti.

wars.name: Bakhtiyar Khalji's conquest of Bihar and Bengal
wars.outcome: Bakhtiyar, a Ghurid general, 'subjugated much of Bihar in 1200' and took Nabadwip about 1203 and Lakhnauti by 1203-1204; Lakshmana Sena fled 'to east Bengal'.

wars.name: Khalji civil war
wars.outcome: Muhammad Shiran Khalji succeeded Bakhtiyar and imprisoned Ali Mardan, who escaped in 1208 and sought help from Aibak ('the first invasion of Bengal by the Delhi Sultanate'); Iwaz governed from 1208, yielded to Ali Mardan about 1210, and declared himself…

wars.name: Iltutmish's conquest of Khalji Bengal
wars.outcome: 1225: Iltutmish invaded and Ghiyasuddin Iwaz paid tribute and accepted his suzerainty; 1227: Nasiruddin Mahmud took Lakhnauti and executed Iwaz.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the extent is the ghurid-dynasty and mamluk-dynasty dossiers' admin-1 unions.
